selectedIdea.title: What the record coral bleaching footprint measures
selectedIdea.description: Use the contrast between the satellite heat-stress footprint and geographically documented bleaching to explain how an event can be record-setting without every exposed reef having a verified outcome.
selectedIdea.rationale: Build the editorial blueprint around the distinction the source makes and explain why it matters to the reader.
selectedIdea.evidence: Exposure area is not the share of reefs that bleached or died. Confirmation date differs from the exposure window. The end date is qualified.

synthesis.content:
### Central insight

Use the contrast between the satellite heat-stress footprint and geographically documented bleaching to explain how an event can be record-setting without every exposed reef having a verified outcome.

### Evidence

NOAA and ICRI confirmed the fourth global bleaching event on April 15, 2024. From January 1, 2023 through September 30, 2025, roughly 84.4% of global coral reef area experienced bleaching-level heat stress. Mass bleaching was documented in at least 83 countries and territories. The previous global event ran from 2014 to 2017 and exposed 68.2% of reef area to bleaching-level heat stress. NOAA’s June 2026 update describes the fourth event as likely having ended in 2025.

### What the narrative should emphasize

Use the contrast between the satellite heat-stress footprint and geographically documented bleaching to explain how an event can be record-setting without every exposed reef having a verified outcome.

### Gaps and uncertainty

Exposure area is not the share of reefs that bleached or died. Confirmation date differs from the exposure window. The end date is qualified.

narrative.content:
### Selected Story
The fourth global coral bleaching event was confirmed in April 2024, while the heat-stress exposure window used to measure its footprint ran from January 2023 through September 2025. The story centers on the distinction between that satellite-measured footprint and geographically documented mass bleaching: roughly 84.4% of global reef area experienced bleaching-level heat stress, while mass bleaching was documented in at least 83 countries and territories. The reader should understand that the large, record-setting exposure footprint measures heat stress—not the share of reefs verified to have bleached or died.

### Story Progression
- **Context:** Introduce the fourth global bleaching event and distinguish its April 2024 confirmation from the January 2023–September 2025 exposure window.
- **Development:** Explain the two measures: roughly 84.4% of global reef area experienced bleaching-level heat stress, compared with mass bleaching documented in at least 83 countries and territories. The previous global event exposed 68.2% of reef area to bleaching-level heat stress.
- **Endpoint:** Clarify that the record-setting footprint is a measure of heat-stress exposure, not a verified bleaching or mortality rate for all exposed reefs. NOAA’s June 2026 update describes the event as likely having ended in 2025.

### Critical Constraints
- Do not equate heat-stress exposure with the share of reefs that bleached or died.
- Keep the confirmation date distinct from the exposure window; describe the event’s 2025 end as likely, not definitive.
